final_text:
Changed `Choice.get_metavar` in `src/click/types.py:261`: when the parameter is an option with `show_choices=False`, the metavar is built from the choices' inferred param type names (`convert_type(None, choice).name.upper()`), de-duplicated in first-seen order via `dict.fromkeys` and joined with `|` — so `["foo", "bar"]` → `[TEXT]`, `[1, 2]` → `[INTEGER]`, `["foo", 1]` → `[TEXT|INTEGER]`. Options with `show_choices=True` and arguments (which have no `show_choices`) keep listing the values, including the `{...}` form for required arguments.

`python -m pytest -q -o pythonpath=src tests/test_options.py` passes: 113 passed. Note the repo's current `tests/test_options.py` contains no `show_choices`/metavar test, so this run exercises no case for the new behavior; I verified the logic by reading `convert_type` rather than executing it (a manual sanity-check command was denied by the sandbox).

Bug report for this repository (click):

An option declared with `type=click.Choice([...])` and `show_choices=False` still shows the
choice values in the `--help` metavar, e.g. `-g [foo|bar]`. With `show_choices=False` the
metavar should show the *type names* of the choices instead — the `name` of the param type each
choice value converts to, upper-cased, de-duplicated in first-seen order, joined with `|`:
`[TEXT]` for string choices, `[INTEGER]` for ints, `[FLOAT]`, `[BOOLEAN]`, and `[TEXT|INTEGER]`
for `["foo", 1]`. Options with `show_choices=True` (the default) and arguments keep showing the
values.

Change as little as possible and do not edit the tests. The test command is
`python -m pytest -q -o pythonpath=src tests/test_options.py`; run it once at the end.
